assessments.quote: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre.
assessments.reason: 2024 bi-centre study on MVI in HCC using enhanced CT nomogram with external CT and MRI validation; abstract evidences CT and MRI modalities and two-centre design, though detailed acquisition parameters are not specified in the abstract.

assessments.quote: This study aims to develop a nomogram model to predict the probability of MVI based on clinical features in HCC patients.
assessments.reason: 2024 nomogram for MVI in HCC but based on clinical features only, single hospital, no CT/MRI acquisition schemes or bi-centre design.

assessments.quote: This retrospective study enrolled 119 patients who underwent DECT liver angiography at 2 medical centres preoperatively.
assessments.reason: 2024 two-centre MVI prediction using dual-energy CT iodine quantification, not a radiological-feature nomogram with CT and MRI; no MRI acquisition and no nomogram.

assessments.quote: These clinical practice guidelines offer updated advice for managing patients with HCC and provide a comprehensive review of pertinent data.
assessments.reason: Clinical practice guideline for HCC management, not a bi-centre imaging nomogram study of MVI with CT/MRI acquisition schemes.

assessments.quote: To develop a clinical-radiomics model using a multimodal machine learning method for distinguishing ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) from breast fibromatosis.
assessments.reason: Breast DCIS vs fibromatosis radiomics study; wrong disease, modality (ultrasound) and task.

assessments.quote: For method validation, we applied it on two datasets (hepatocellular carcinoma and locally advanced rectal cancer) imaged by different modalities
assessments.reason: Method for peritumour transition-zone analysis; not an MVI nomogram and does not report CT/MRI acquisition schemes or bi-centre MVI design.
Conference abstract book; no evidence of the requested MVI bi-centre CT/MRI nomogram study.
